channel.title: Open-Xchange — recent CVEs
channel.description: Most recent CVEs assigned by Open-Xchange (ox).

item.title: CVE-2026-124727 · 6.5 MEDIUM 🌩️ — AXFR of obsolete record types can corrupt zones in the Bind backend
item.description: Incorrect handling of obsolete record types during zone AXFR to Bind backend will cause the zone to fail to load afterwards, requiring manual intervention to edit the zone file.

item.title: CVE-2026-124728 · 7.5 HIGH 🌩️ — TSIG operation logic flaws
item.description: Incomplete GSS negotiation, as well as TKEY context deletion while a pending operation will need to be signed with that key, can lead to a crash.

item.title: CVE-2026-123764 · 7.5 HIGH 🌩️ — Injection vulnerabilities in Bind backend
item.description: Incorrect sanitization of received data during zone AXFR to Bind backend can cause wrong or invalid data to be serialized.

item.title: CVE-2026-123757 · 7.4 HIGH 🌩️ — Incomplete domain name sanitization during Bind autosecondary zone transfer
item.description: An attacker can send a notify request that causes the root zone to be added as a secondary domain to be added to the bind backend, but causes said backend to update its configuration to an invalid one, leading to the backend no longer able to run on…

item.title: CVE-2026-123758 · 4.4 MEDIUM — Race condition in forward notification handling
item.description: A race condition in the handling of the forward notification requests queue can lead to a crash if too many UDP notify packets for a given zone are received in a short time frame.

item.title: CVE-2026-123759 · 4.8 MEDIUM 🌩️ — Catalog zones incorrectly accept the root zone as a member
item.description: A catalog zone provider can add a root zone as member and cause PowerDNS to provision it from the given source.

item.title: CVE-2026-123760 · 6.5 MEDIUM — Logic flaw in LMDB backend can lead to an unresponsive server
item.description: When using the LMDB backend, performing zone rectification when the number of Empty Non-Terminal entries is larger than the max-ent-entries setting triggers a logic bug and causes the PowerDNS process to spin with the LMDB database locked.

item.title: CVE-2026-123762 · 7.6 HIGH — Catalog zone update operation may misbehave in multi-backend configurations
item.description: A catalog zone update introducing a new zone which already exists, but in a different backend than the one storing the catalog zone, will cause a duplicate zone to be created in that backend, and (depending on the backend load order) may completely h…

item.title: CVE-2026-123761 · 8.2 HIGH 🌩️ — Multiple defects in Views processing
item.description: Various logic errors in view processing can cause incorrect cached results to be returned.

item.title: CVE-2026-85566 · 4.8 MEDIUM 🌩️ — EDNS option or DNS record smuggling
item.description: An attacker might be able to forge its own source IP, smuggle DNS records or bypass EDNS options filtering via a specially crafted DNS query when EDNS Client Subnet is enabled between DNSdist and its backend.

item.title: CVE-2026-85565 · 3.1 LOW — Denial of service via oversized DoH query
item.description: An attacker can trigger a synchronization issue on outgoing TCP connections between DNSdist and its backend by sending oversized DNS over HTTPS queries. This could cause the backend to refuse queries, send a server failure, or just close the TCP conn…

item.title: CVE-2026-85564 · 4.3 MEDIUM — Finished QUIC streams should not linger around
item.description: An attacker can trigger a large memory use by cancelling QUIC streams while DNSdist is retrieving the response from its backend. Instead of releasing the memory corresponding to the cancelled stream right away, DNSdist was mistakenly keeping it aroun…

item.title: CVE-2026-85562 · 5.3 MEDIUM 🌩️ — Duplicate X-Forwarded-For DNS over HTTPS headers are not properly handled
item.description: When DNS over HTTPS is enabled and configured to trust incoming X-Forwarded-For headers, and the reverse proxy placed in front of DNSdist does not replace existing X-Forwarded-For headers but merely append a new header to the query, the first header…

item.title: CVE-2026-85561 · 5.4 MEDIUM 🌩️ — Wrong remote DoH client IP passed to proxy-protocol-enabled backend
item.description: When DNS over HTTPS is enabled and configured to trust incoming X-Forwarded-For headers, in addition to the use of the proxy protocol being enabled between DNSdist and one of its backends, an outgoing TCP connection could be wrongly reused for a quer…

item.title: CVE-2026-123756 · 4.3 MEDIUM — Insufficient input validation of internal webserver
item.description: An attacker can cause a denial of service by sending crafted HTTP queries to the internal webserver. The webserver is not enabled by default and is protected by an ACL.

item.title: CVE-2026-123755 · 4.3 MEDIUM — Crafted zone transfer can freeze an outgoing TCP connection
item.description: An attacker allowed to send AXFR or IXFR queries can cause an outgoing TCP connection to the backend to be stuck, causing a denial of service to other clients trying to reuse the same outgoing connection.

item.title: CVE-2026-85567 · 3.1 LOW — Empty API key should disable the API
item.description: Setting an empty API key was not properly disabling access to the internal HTTP API, despite being documented as such. This allowed an attacker whose IP address was allowed by the webserver ACL to bypass the authentication and get read-only access to…

item.title: CVE-2026-85563 · 4.2 MEDIUM — HTTP body should not be processed on DNS over HTTPS GET queries
item.description: When DNS over HTTPS is enabled and a caching HTTP reverse proxy is used in front of DNSdist, it is possible to pollute the cache of the HTTP reverse proxy by sending DNS over HTTPS GET queries with a body. DNSdist should either refuse the query or ig…

item.title: CVE-2026-52688 · 7.5 HIGH 🌩️ — RRSIGs with too few labels can lead to bypass of DNSSEC wildcard validation
item.description: RRSIGs with too few labels can lead to bypass of DNSSEC wildcard validation

item.title: CVE-2026-52686 · 3.7 LOW 🌩️ — Wildcard CNAME proof validation bypass
item.description: The issue is a DNSSEC validation bypass where wildcard expansion proofs (NSEC/NSEC3 records) are accepted without signature validation when the wildcard answer is a CNAME or DNAME record.

item.title: CVE-2026-52684 · 3.7 LOW 🌩️ — Prefetch Feature Allows Persistent Ghost Domain Cache Poisoning Attack

item.title: CVE-2026-42389 · 5.3 MEDIUM 🌩️ — Reject more queries with invalid header values
item.description: This fix provides extra hardening for the 5.4.x branch by doing extra validation of incoming answers from authoritative servers.

item.title: CVE-2026-52690 · 5.9 MEDIUM 🌩️ — Spoofed answers can mark an authoritative non-EDNS capable
item.description: Spoofing replies to Recursor might mark an IP of an authoritative server as not supporting EDNS, causing valdiation of DNSSEC records served by that server to fail.

item.title: CVE-2026-42390 · 5.3 MEDIUM 🌩️ — ZONEMD validation can be bypassed
item.description: An invalid zone might pass ZONEMD validation while it should not. This is only relevant if ZoneToCache is configured with ZONEMD validation.

item.title: CVE-2026-42388 · 5.9 MEDIUM 🌩️ — Missing input validation for catalog zones
item.description: Incomplete validation of the SOA record present in a catalog zone might lead to a crash.
